T-002 (2026-11-02): mount-path feasibility PROVEN — no owner escalation needed. Method: the bench page exposes the live instance and engine class (window.__BENCH_EDITOR/__BENCH_MUYA, src/renderer/bench/main.js, bench-scope diff committed with this evidence); a driver-side probe mounts a second isolated instance whose model is parsed whole (importMarkdown only) and whose DOM mounts in top-level block ranges — initial region via stateRender.render(slice), each next range via stateRender.partialRender(slice anchored at the last mounted block key, endKey null). Results (Chromium, same-run legacy reference): mixed-100k (367 blocks) legacy open 82 ms; progressive firstPaint 18-57 ms, every range under 51 ms; size-1mb (3,706 blocks) legacy open 551 ms (mount 496 ms); progressive firstPaint 25-68 ms, initial 100-block region 10.6-11 ms, per-range median ~13 ms with occasional ~100 ms spikes (GC/layout; the T-003 slice budget yields between ranges and the 300 ms longest-task ceiling holds), total mount work ~490-540 ms — the same work, never in one blocking chunk. Canonical Markdown byte-identical and DOM top-level block count exact on all eight chunk-size runs (PASS=true across 50/100/200/400 on both fixtures). Sync-region decision from measurement: the synchronous region is the first 100 blocks (about 11 ms at both shapes) extended to cover the viewport, and the background chunk size is 50-100 blocks — replacing the plan's working default (larger of 2 viewports or 40 blocks) with the measured numbers. Design findings recorded for T-003: (a) stateRender.render's root lookup document.querySelector('div#ag-editor-id') is a document-global singleton — a second live instance patches the first instance's DOM and leaves its own container empty; never exercised in the app (only one Muya exists; split view is editor+preview), but the progressive seam must target its own container and any second-instance test must isolate (the probe removes the prior root first); (b) the anchored-extension pattern (startKey = last mounted block, slice inclusive, endKey null) is the range primitive; (c) partialRender needs a non-empty activeBlocks — the anchor block works and suppresses the cursor patch. Probe was ephemeral (not committed); the bench exposure diff is the only product-tree change.
